summary: Nolorim, the pass-wardens of the high valleys: stone and watch-fires in the passes, kin who send wardens, eyes on the south and east, and a guest-house for the hidden heir.

wardens_oath.name: The Wardens' Oath
wardens_oath.desc: A short oath, sworn on a stone from the first tower, binds every warden to his post.

wardens_first_spirit.name: Wardens First
wardens_first_spirit.desc: The towers take the best of the valleys' young, and they dig in as if they meant to stay.

valleys_first_spirit.name: Valleys First
valleys_first_spirit.desc: Well-fed valleys, mended terraces and busy quarries.

heights_watch.name: Watchtowers on the Heights
heights_watch.desc: Towers above towers: no road below is hidden for long.

southern_eyes.name: Eyes on the South
southern_eyes.desc: Scouts on the southern ridges see far and report quickly.

herders.name: Herders of the Heights
herders.desc: Goatherds know every path of the mountain and every man who walks it.

hold_every_pass_spirit.name: Hold Every Pass
hold_every_pass_spirit.desc: Every pass has its company, every company its tower.

no_road.name: No Road Through Nolorim
no_road.desc: The gates are shut, the stones are ready, and the wardens are in their places.

the_pass_wardens.title: The Towers Count Their Wardens
the_pass_wardens.desc: At the spring muster Nolwe counts the wardens in each tower, and the count is short in every one. The old men ask whether to light every tower with what there is, or to rebuild the near ones properly and leave the far ones to the wind.

nolorim_asks_kin.title: Nolorim Asks for Wardens
nolorim_asks_kin.desc: A rider from the high valleys of Nolorim reaches the council with a plain request: wardens for the towers on the passes, for a season, as a kindness between kin. The council weighs it against the needs of its own borders.

nolorim_asks_the_forest.title: Nolorim Asks the Forest
nolorim_asks_the_forest.desc: A herald of Nolorim stands in the great forest's hall and asks the elders for a company of wardens to stand a year in the high passes. The elders know the towers are old, and the herald's boots are worn.

herders_report.title: Herders Report
herders_report.desc: The herders of the heights come down with a story. Strangers with good boots measured the high road with knotted cords, and they paid for goat's milk in coin from across the eastern water. Nolwe has the report copied twice, and the second copy sent west.

focuses.name: The Pass-Wardens of Nolorim
focuses.desc: Two high valleys, a handful of watch-towers and a federation of pass-wardens under Nolwe. The towers are old and half-manned, and nobody has come through them in arms for a very long time.

focuses.name: Nolwe's Watch
focuses.desc: Pass-Warden Nolwe walks the whole length of the border each spring and counts every tower, every beacon and every man. He has not yet been pleased by the count.

focuses.name: The Federated Valleys
focuses.desc: The two valleys keep one moot and two hearths. Their herders quarrel over water, their wardens over precedence, and both agree that the passes matter more than either.

focuses.name: The Wardens' Oath
focuses.desc: Every warden of the high passes swears the same short oath on a stone from the first tower: to keep the watch, to light the flame and to leave the post only when relieved.

focuses.name: Wardens First
focuses.desc: The best of the valleys' young are drawn to the towers, and the herds and quarries get what is left. The passes will be held, whatever the valleys must give up.

focuses.name: Valleys First
focuses.desc: The valleys come first: the herds are fattened, the terraces mended and the quarries worked. A well-fed warden is a long-lived one.

focuses.name: Nolorim Endures
focuses.desc: The smallest of the Magical Lands' realms has held its passes since before the Wall was built. It sees no reason to stop now.

focuses.name: Stone in the Passes
focuses.desc: Quarrymen cut stone from the foot of the Magic Mountains and haul it by goat-track to the high towers. Every block laid in the passes is a year of safety bought.

focuses.name: Watchtowers on the Heights
focuses.desc: New towers are raised on the heights above the old ones, and the watchers in them see farther down the roads than their fathers ever did.

focuses.name: The High Roads
focuses.desc: The goat-tracks between the towers are widened and paved, so that a warden may reach the next post in an hour rather than a day.

focuses.name: Walls Across the Passes
focuses.desc: Where the passes are narrowest the pass-wardens raise walls of dry stone, four paces thick and five high, with a single gate that can be barred from within.

focuses.name: The Magic Mountains Road
focuses.desc: A road is cut along the flank of the Magic Mountains, joining Nolorim's valleys to the lands of the kin. It is steep and cold, and kinder than the old way.

focuses.name: Beacons to the Kin
focuses.desc: A chain of beacons is raised from the high passes to the great groves, so that the kin may see the flame and know the passes are being held.

focuses.name: Ask the Kin
focuses.desc: Nolorim sends heralds to the three realms that think best of it, asking for wardens to stand a season in the towers. A few fathers have already answered.

focuses.name: Wardens from the Forest
focuses.desc: A message goes to the elders of the Magical Forest: the passes are old, the towers few, and a company of the forest's wardens would be gladly housed.

focuses.name: Kin Beacons
focuses.desc: Beacon-keepers from the kin's groves come to teach the pass-wardens their fire-signals, and take back the signals Nolorim has learned for itself.

focuses.name: The Kindred at the Passes
focuses.desc: The Kindred of the Woods has been raised, and Nolorim takes its place at last among the kin, with the high passes as its share of the common defence.

focuses.name: Eyes on the South
focuses.desc: Scouts are set on the southern ridges to watch the roads below. They have seen merchants, pilgrims and, once, a very lost bear.

focuses.name: The Eastern Approaches
focuses.desc: The herders speak of strangers on the high road who measured the ground with cords and paid for goat's milk in coin from across the water. Nolwe orders the report copied and sent west.

focuses.name: The Southern Road Watch
focuses.desc: A small fort is raised where the southern road enters the valley, with a gate, a well and barracks for forty. It is the first new stonework in Nolorim in two centuries.

focuses.name: Herders of the Heights
focuses.desc: The goatherds of the heights are organised in bands, each with a horn and a beacon. They see everything on the mountain and have always said so to anyone who would listen.

focuses.name: A Guest in the Passes
focuses.desc: A weary traveller has come over the high pass, asking for nothing but a roof, and [zin_loc_eindil] is shown to the warden's own hearth. The pass-wardens do not ask whom they shelter.

focuses.name: Hide the Guest
focuses.desc: The guest is lodged in a cave behind the oldest tower, where no stranger's eye can find him. The towers know every path, and the paths keep silent.

focuses.name: The Mountain Paths
focuses.desc: Pass-wardens guide the guest over goat-tracks that save weeks of travel. Nobody on those heights has ever been late to a place they meant to reach.

focuses.name: Pass Companies
focuses.desc: The wardens of the towers are drawn into companies, each posted to a pass and drilled to hold it. They know every rock and every drift.

focuses.name: Mountain Bows
focuses.desc: Short, stiff bows are cut for shooting down steep slopes, strung with goat-gut and tipped with chipped flint. They are poor weapons on a plain and deadly on a ridge.

focuses.name: Stone-Throwers
focuses.desc: Counterweight throwers are built on the gate-towers, to roll stone down on any host that comes up the narrow road in column.

focuses.name: Hold Every Pass
focuses.desc: Every pass has its company, every company its tower and every tower its beacon. Nolorim, which has never seemed formidable, becomes a hard place to enter.

focuses.name: The Passes Hold
focuses.desc: The beacons burn from tower to tower. An armed host is on the road, and Nolorim's old gates are closed for the first time in living memory.

focuses.name: No Road Through Nolorim
focuses.desc: The pass-wardens swear that no road shall run through Nolorim for as long as there is a stone to roll and a warden to roll it.

focuses.name: The Kin Send More
focuses.desc: Wardens from the kin's groves march up the long road to the passes, their packs heavy with arrows and their hearts lighter than they were.

focuses.name: The Passes Are Quiet
focuses.desc: The road below is empty and the beacons are dark. The wardens climb back to their towers and begin, as always, to count the stones.
